## Problem List

1. Complete the selected-export semantic/admission boundary and structural Identity coverage remaining from #44.
2. Complete justified native calls/data/control for the selected C boundary remaining from #49.

Disposition successor, 2026-10-03. This consolidates **unfinished** C-backend work from [#44](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/issues/44) and [#49](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/issues/49); superseding them does not claim their residuals were implemented. Keep their original bodies/comments as provenance. Both sections use the existing **c-backend** owner and [one owning work list](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/blob/09ee7750604f1de2264dd4dad5ab5f174583c655/doc/2026-10-03-C-BACKEND-GOAL.md). Merge coordinates shared boundaries and integration; no replacement worker or additional implementation plan is created.

### P1. Selected-export semantics and structural realization

#### Subjective (User)

Original English paraphrases in #44, 2026-09-28: implement Artifact-to-C first, preserve backend-independent semantics, checked facts/residual obligations and explicit target contracts. Subsequent owner clarification recorded in the backend README: `.a` serves A Program; LinkerScript, target ABI/representation and realization stay downstream. This successor is an agent consolidation under the human issue-disposition assignment, not approval of new admission/erasure rules.

#### Objective (Code)

Inspected Main `09ee7750604f1de2264dd4dad5ab5f174583c655`: the prototype imports `.a`, borrows typed roots and emits buildable structural C for a documented subset, with closures, exact host arithmetic/Text/effects and constructor/Match differentials. Packaging #46 is delivered. [Adapter](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/blob/09ee7750604f1de2264dd4dad5ab5f174583c655/src/prototype/c_backend/main.c#L125) still requires ordinary whole-module revalidation or explicit unauthenticated completed-module trust. [Contract](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/blob/09ee7750604f1de2264dd4dad5ab5f174583c655/src/prototype/c_backend/README.md) retains dependent thunk lifting, iterated higher actions and arbitrary U/Pi Identity limits. Structural Acc QuickSort `FFTT` is delivered; native sorting is separate.

C11 task `56e4ae8` fixes publication stream-error classification and preserves failed-output cleanup. Its [handoff](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/blob/56e4ae8/doc/2026-10-03-C-BACKEND-EPOCH11-HANDOFF.md) pins worker C9/E8 results. Merge additionally reports thirteen current E9+E10 backend gates and nineteen I/O assertions passing; that report is distinct from this audit's fresh code/record inspection and the older worker producer. No new runtime gate ran in this issue audit.

#### Assessment

The initial C subset is delivered. Per-export admissibility and broader Identity remain. General relevance and pending-proof policy stay in **#47**; this section implements an explicitly justified boundary after that design, rather than deciding it by closing #44. Whole-source exact-frontier restoration remains SE/AP work, not a reason to withhold an otherwise supported C export.

#### Plan

- [ ] Specify/query selected-export lowerability using existing typed transport/nominal descriptors, distinguishing verified source facts, residual obligations, target support and lowering assumptions. Sufficient material must not require mandatory further Solve; insufficient/pending/rejected information must report explicit not-ready/refusal under the chosen #47 contract.
- [ ] Implement justified remaining dependent/higher Identity cases, retaining computational witnesses, neutral cases and explicit unsupported boundaries.
- [ ] Preserve completed/pending/corrupt-image, nominal-family/descriptor round-trip, overflow, closures/calls, effect order, runtime/I/O failure and evaluator-differential controls. Emitter stays inert; imported bytes/status flags do not manufacture evidence.
- [ ] Keep bounded Nat transformations downstream with whole-reachable-value invariants and explicit prove/check-fallback/assume policy. A trapping bound is not exact unbounded-Nat behavior; approximation needs explicit opt-in. CUDA/RTL and future recurrence remain separate later work.

### P2. Target-native selected-boundary realization

#### Subjective (User)

Original English paraphrase in #49, 2026-09-29: produce C-oriented native computation, including QuickSort, with Link Manifest selecting exports and realization. Readable target C is the owner's Tradition motivation, not source semantics or a license to replace programs by source names. Preserve this separately from P1's semantic/admission contract.

#### Objective (Code)

Scalar ABI/direct shared calls, nominal enum/data/nested records, transitive known captures, transactional array helpers and selected applied List/Nat instances are delivered prototypes. C9 task `60c100c`/Main `48c42eb` has [thirteen pinned Root E8 O2 gates](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/blob/09ee7750604f1de2264dd4dad5ab5f174583c655/src/prototype/c_backend/verification/core-epoch9.json); C10 task `fe497956`/Main `2753441` supplies ordinary-module client evidence. Worker-client sanitizer scope remains separate. Indexed SizedList, callable/recursive Acc fields and native Acc/QuickSort are still unsupported; dynamic callbacks/demanded effects, recursive captures and general nominal exchange remain explicit limits.

#### Assessment

Continue the existing bounded representation work before native sorting. A List array helper, structural `FFTT`, source Sortedness, finite differential tests or the historical 53-line hand-derived template is not a native lowering correctness proof. #52 checked equality reuse remains a separate optional optimization boundary.

#### Plan

- [ ] Specify checked applicability, observable input/result domain, ABI/ownership/resource contract and semantic-versus-executable dependency closure for each supported profile. Preserve the single downstream LinkerScript, required private/foreign/effect dependencies and explicit native-only refusal/fallback policy. Any precomputation is budgeted and justified by checked facts; emission must preserve open/effectful behavior without forcing arbitrary NF or executing source I/O.
- [ ] Extend justified representations/control/call lowering to indexed/callable shapes needed by native Acc/QuickSort; preserve partial application, captures, demand/effect order. Retain bounded reusable length/append/partition controls before claiming the sorter.
- [ ] Give Acc/relevance transformations and source-to-target sortedness/permutation transfer an explicit applicability/refinement argument. Preserve nominal generativity; shared layout or source-name/hash matching grants no semantics.
- [ ] Preserve constants/open functions/effects/private callees/callbacks/partial applications/unsupported controls, inert deterministic emission, immutable `.a`, source/interpreter/native differentials and relevant sanitizer gates. Record transformations, assumptions, unsupported reasons and fallback in downstream receipts; separate coverage from performance claims.

Completion: both residual sections meet their stated contracts with pinned verification and explicit remaining assumptions, without a second canonical semantic owner or hidden admission weakening. Prototype publication/integration and accepted promotion remain separate stages. #43 recurrence, #47 relevance, #51 ownership gates, #52 equality reuse and SE/AP checkpoint repair retain their own decisions/requirements.
title: C backend residuals: selected-export admission, Identity and native lowering

body:
## Problem and requested outcome

The owner supplied a detailed Test-Suite Growth / Verification Debt audit and
requested an Issue and documentation PR on 2026-10-03. Track the audit as a
**verification/process architecture problem**, not a request to delete tests or
weaken compiler acceptance.

Implementation progress, prototype integration, accepted promotion, permanent
semantic coverage and per-epoch reproducibility machinery need separate metrics.
Repeated use of a fixture may protect distinct contracts; equal filenames do not
establish duplicate tests. Conversely, growing manifests/gates/docs must not be
counted as increased language capability.

Inspection baseline: **37de1e8ca0d163e4d139ac70caafa19fae2142f9**.
This is a current-head static review, not a fresh runtime/coverage experiment.

## Confirmed current observations

1. `src/Makefile:80` composes `check-acceptance` from broad and specialized gates;
   later declarations add more prerequisites. The same examples occur in
   `check-examples`, `syntax_io_test` (line 158), `parse_files` (line 456), and
   `check-example-results`. Parsing, syntax round-trip, admission and result
   equality are different candidate obligations, not proven duplication.
2. `tests/quick_result.sh`, `generic_sorted.sh`, `retained_quicksort.sh`,
   `local_strong_sorted.sh`, `image_cli.sh`, and `compatibility.sh` contain
   related save/load/pending/retained flows around sorting and proof fixtures.
   Their semantic assertions differ, while some lifecycle mechanics recur.
3. `tests/compatibility.sh` explicitly enables `--legacy-intrinsic-dot`, uses
   archived fixtures, and also checks current image/result semantics. It is
   currently 400 lines; size is an inventory clue, not a redundancy verdict.
4. `tests/compatibility.tsv` records `review_pending`; `tests/inventory.sh`
   generates a frozen historical capability inventory. `syntax_inventory.sh`
   reads program rows and explicitly says syntax expectations are **not semantic
   acceptance**. These are not a unified effective-invocation/property/lifecycle
   inventory. Other owner/structural inventories exist and must not be ignored.
5. No tracked `src/prototype/test_audit/` inventory was found at this revision.
   No existing unified test-obligation/cost/lifecycle ledger was found in the
   inspected entrypoints. This is a scoped observation, not an assertion that
   no useful verification inventory exists anywhere.
6. Current coordination records actual setup/transport/report interruptions:
   omitted training inputs, wrong `eval.h` assembly, TSV newline/hash changes,
   a migration-column setup error, and incomplete worker assembly. These are
   recorded failures, not newly reproduced compiler failures in this audit.

## Snapshot corrections and existing positive work

The supplied audit describes prototype checkpoint `435d965` and E1 integration.
The latest coordination plan instead records reviewed prototype Main `7b27c4c`,
with **Job E2 integrated**, E3/E4 still separately qualifying and C6 awaiting its
current-producer integration. Accepted semantic baseline remains `eb0aad6`.
A path-limited diff finds no accepted `src/` (excluding `src/prototype/`),
`tests/`, or README changes between that baseline and the inspection revision.

The latest plan **already has** a Current Delivery Status table and requires
issue-linked worker feedback distinguishing implementation, local/joint
verification, publication and integration. Extend it; do not claim progress
reporting starts from zero or invent a parallel authority/second work list.

`src/prototype/solver_inputs/joint_verification/e2-broad-summary.json` reports
384 O2 recipes and 45 sanitizer commands, plus three unwaived strict reload
cases: `1000:1000`, `1600:1600`, `1915:0`. These are repository-reported results,
**not fresh passes/failures from this audit**, and recipe counts are not counts
of independent semantic contracts. It explicitly disclaims promotion, issue
completion and measured wall/RSS improvement.

## Proposed workstreams (TA1–TA8)

- **TA1/TA8 — Progress ledger:** separate accepted/prototype runtime deltas,
  test/docs/report deltas, removed/added owners/state, promotion backlog,
  known-failure movement and measured-versus-unmeasured cost.
- **TA2 — Semantic inventory:** map effective invocation → property/boundary →
  lifecycle/owner/producer/cost. Classify exact duplicates, semantic duplicate
  candidates, orthogonal reuse, regression witnesses and harness/meta tests.
- **TA3 — Legacy classification:** give each default archived-fixture dependency
  a deliberate compatibility/current-regression/historical retention reason;
  `review_pending` is not a mandate to restore every old behavior.
- **TA4 — First pilot:** QuickSort/sortedness/persistence overlap matrix. Preserve
  LocalSorted, StrongSorted, ordinary-result, rejection, byte identity, NF and
  pending/resume as distinct obligations. Consolidate mechanics only after
  demonstrating coverage preservation.
- **TA5 — Verification debt:** distinguish semantic/crash/sanitizer failures
  from harness/assembly/transport/report/environment failures. Minimize copied
  artifacts while retaining sufficient reproducibility and original failures.
- **TA6 — Advisory audit lane:** propose a read-mostly `verification-audit` role,
  with docs and prototype-only audit tools. Core/user retain decisions about
  promotion and permanent test retirement. This Issue does not launch a worker.
- **TA7 — Lifecycle:** current-contract, regression-witness,
  compatibility-contract, audit-only, epoch-only, superseded and historical.
  Specify promotion/retirement decisions instead of retaining epoch gates forever.

## Guardrails

- First epoch is inventory and proposals only: **no accepted tests/Makefile/source
  edits, deletion, expectation relaxation or waiver of known failures**.
- One property may legitimately need multiple small witnesses, independent
  oracles or large integration cases. Matching property IDs alone is not proof
  of equivalent coverage.
- Reuse old gate results only under a sufficient reproducibility key: actual
  producer/binary, flags/toolchain, dependent inputs/harness/generator, relevant
  environment, policy/seed and options. Source/fixture/command hash equality
  alone is not generally sufficient. Changed producers require affected gates
  and a final joint qualification as appropriate.
- Thresholds in the supplied proposal (20% runtime growth, consecutive epochs,
  etc.) are review triggers to decide, not automatic stop/delete rules.
- No broad suite rerun merely to publish this audit; cost measurement should be
  a separate pinned exclusive pass, coordinated with performance work.
- Do not build another large harness bureaucracy. Start with one small inventory
  and one pilot, reuse existing manifests/progress reports, then justify expansion.

## First-epoch completion criteria

- [ ] Define current accepted vs assembled-Prototype suite entrypoints and scope.
- [ ] Map the effective invocation graph with property, lifecycle and owner.
- [ ] Classify default `archive/legacy/` dependencies with explicit reasons.
- [ ] Produce QuickSort/persistence matrix and exact duplicate candidates;
  manually review semantic candidates and orthogonal reuse.
- [ ] Measure actual current-producer cost once in a controlled slot; do not
  infer runtime from LOC, gate count or old worker results.
- [ ] Extend the existing delivery table with verification debt and structural
  deltas, without conflating prototype integration with accepted promotion.
- [ ] Preserve known failures, negative controls and unique regression witnesses.
- [ ] Publish keep/consolidate/archive recommendations with loss-of-coverage
  analysis; obtain explicit approval before permanent suite changes.

Related: #51 (reproducible size/semantic-owner gates), #56 (checker performance),
#52 (checked equality reuse). This Issue adds suite-debt/progress accountability;
it does not replace those implementation tasks or close them.

The supporting documentation-only [PR #60](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/pull/60) preserves
`doc/2026-10-03-TEST-SUITE-GROWTH-AND-PROGRESS-AUDIT.md` with a dated current-head
cover. Publication itself does not complete this audit's substantive criteria.
title: Audit verification debt: semantic test inventory, lifecycle and implementation progress accounting

body:
## Summary

Function Graph named-case selectors use `sourceSelector := localBinder`, the
opposite of ordinary A Program binding. This is a confirmed surface-language
design inconsistency, reproduced on accepted source and the latest
`solver_inputs` overlay at **eb0aad673dd0fb5219eb0d720d45a819cc50edba**.

It survived the pointer-core rewrite. It is not, on this evidence, a demonstrated
kernel-unsoundness bug. The proposed double-brace named set is not implemented.

The project owner requested publication of this audit on 2026-10-03. Publication
does not itself settle every grammar/compatibility choice in the supplied proposal.

## Current behavior and reproduction

Use `tests/acceptance/function-graph-named-fields.p`, which defines `length` with
source recursive-result binder `tailLength`:

```ap
@cons { tailLength := recursive; } => Nat.succ *recursive
```

Current compilation resolves LHS `tailLength` as source metadata and introduces
RHS `recursive` into branch scope. Ordinary block `lhs := rhs` instead introduces
the LHS. This exception complicates reading, source migration and scope tooling.

Build at the pinned revision:

```sh
make -f src/Makefile BUILD=/tmp/ap-named-accepted \
  /tmp/ap-named-accepted/pointer-check /tmp/ap-named-accepted/program_test
bash src/prototype/solver_inputs/overlay.sh /tmp/ap-named-candidate
make -f /tmp/ap-named-candidate/src/Makefile BUILD=/tmp/ap-named-candidate/build \
  /tmp/ap-named-candidate/build/pointer-check \
  /tmp/ap-named-candidate/build/program_test
```

The overlay destination must not exist. Run each checker with `--steps 10000000`
on the original fixture and separate controlled copies:

| Fixture edit | Accepted result | Latest Prototype result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | DONE, 13,353 steps | DONE, 9,396 steps |
| Replace `tailLength := recursive` with `recursive := tailLength` everywhere; keep body references | REJECTED, 9,961 steps | REJECTED, 7,161 steps |
| Replace `{ tailLength := recursive; }` with `{{ tailLength := recursive; }}` | Parse error: expected named selector | Same parse error |
| Replace `{ tail; tailLength := recursive; }` with `{ tailLength := recursive; tail; }` | DONE, 13,353 steps | DONE, 9,396 steps |

Also verified `main`, `aliasMain`, `graphMain`, `valueMain`, and reordered
`graphMain` against `expected`, using `program_test --equal` with chunks 1 and 64
on both builds. Existing duplicate-selector and wrong-proof negative fixtures
remain rejected. This is focused verification, not a full acceptance-suite pass.

## Code and historical evidence

- `src/syntax.c`: elimination parser stores first identifier in `item.name` and
  the post-`:=` identifier as the expression atom.
- `src/synthesis.c:case_field_scope`: resolves `item.name` as source selector and
  binds `item.expression->token` as local alias. Latest overlay retains this.
- `src/syntax.c:mark_index_names`: clause scope scanning also treats RHS as local;
  changing just parser/elaborator would leave an inconsistent consumer.
- Current field-array/telescope expansion already respects canonical dependent
  order and hides omitted fields. Single-brace source order is currently ignored.
- `src/syntax_io.c`: persisted clause-item validation is another migration boundary.
- README documents generated graph types and ordinary brace constructs, but not
  this named Function Graph selector grammar.
- Historical design in PR #21 explicitly specified `selector := localName`.
  Commit `4fe5aee` stores separate source/local symbol IDs in that direction;
  its fixture uses `tailLength := recursive` then `@recursive`. This is an
  inherited design choice, not a recent accidental parser regression.

## Requested design correction

Prefer one consistent binding invariant:

```ap
@cons {{ recursive := tailLength; }} => Nat.succ *recursive
```

Here LHS is a local binder; RHS resolves only against the selected function
owner/case's source-origin metadata. One selected origin can expose local value,
`@local` graph and valid `*local` IH roles. Keep positional patterns available.

**Separate the decisions:** reversing polarity addresses the confirmed issue;
adding unordered `{{...}}` and canonically ordered `{...}` is an additional
proposal. Strict single-brace ordering would reject currently valid reordered
proofs and adds a proof-ABI dependency on generated field order. Decide and
document this deliberately rather than describe it as existing behavior.

Unordered selection must not create an unordered dependent Context. Reuse the
existing complete canonical telescope, hidden fields and role associations;
do not introduce a second Context/telescope implementation or new GlobalNames.

Do not accept both directions using selector-availability heuristics: both sides
can be valid source names. Choose an explicit migration/version contract and
diagnose likely legacy syntax without silently rewriting its meaning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide corrected polarity and whether both brace modes are required.
- [ ] Migrate parser/AST, elaborator and all binding/scope-scan consumers together.
- [ ] Test distinct-name renaming; identity shorthand alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Test unordered permutation, ordered subsequences/reversal if adopted,
  unknown/duplicate selectors and duplicate local names.
- [ ] Test both-valid-selector ambiguity, lexical scope policy, `@local` and
  `*local` validity/association, omitted dependent fields and IH construction.
- [ ] Preserve complete canonical Match lowering; test elaborated evidence, not
  just equal output on a closed example.
- [ ] Version or reject old persisted syntax where required; cover source/image
  round-trips and reload without reinterpreting historical aliases.
- [ ] Migrate active fixtures/docs/examples atomically; preserve historical docs.
- [ ] Document source-origin selector naming as a proof-facing API and add README
  grammar. Run full relevant acceptance/compatibility/persistence gates.

## Supporting documents

The documentation-only [PR #58](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/pull/58) contains:

- `doc/2026-10-03-FUNCTION-GRAPH-NAMED-BINDER-SYNTAX-AUDIT.md` (supplied proposal,
  preserved with a current-head qualification).
- `doc/2026-10-03-NEW-AUDITS-CURRENT-HEAD-REVIEW.md` (fresh execution results and
  additional migration boundaries).

The documentation PR does not implement or resolve this Issue.
title: Correct Function Graph named-binding polarity and define explicit syntax migration

## Summary

At **eb0aad673dd0fb5219eb0d720d45a819cc50edba**, accepted A Program and the latest
`solver_inputs` overlay still eagerly materialize demanded intermediate heads,
copy suspended argument prefixes, and build administrative lambdas to apply
IADT branch fields. These are concrete optimization targets that remain despite
newer Job/Evidence owner consolidation.

The supplied Bend comparison reports promising experiments, but they are pinned
to **9146893f07f0fe3f4c8309c370420c1702dfb96d plus an experimental overlay**.
This Issue requests **current-head reproduction, profiling and safe recovery**,
not automatic promotion of those patches or a claim of measured current slowdown.

The project owner requested publication on 2026-10-03 and considers these
foundational concerns important. No proof-soundness defect is established here.

## Confirmed current implementation mechanisms

| Mechanism | Source / observation on accepted and latest Prototype |
| --- | --- |
| Eager intermediate readback | `src/eval.c:resume_frame` runs `pg_materialize_step` before a continuation receives a `const pg_term *` answer. |
| Suspended argument prefix copying | `pg_eval_frame_copy_argument` copies links until the demanded target is replaced with the materialized answer. |
| Administrative IADT application | `src/iadt.c:apply_fields` creates `lambda k. k fields...` and applies it to the captured branch closure. |
| Small-owner allocation minima | `src/graph.c:pg_alloc` uses at least `512 * sizeof(max_align_t)` bytes per arena block; `pg_index_init` starts at 64 buckets. |
| One-transition scheduler wrapping | `src/synthesis_conversion.c` advances WHNF by budget 1, checks its certificate, and re-enqueues pending work. |
| Repeated checking-input projection | `normalization_step` retrieves `pg_evidence_subject(checking_term)->core` each time; currently this accessor is a small switch/direct pointer read, not evidence of term copying. |

The actual costs, owner lifetimes and reuse frequency need profiling on current
HEAD. Presence of a code path does not establish its wall-time contribution.

Both current binaries were freshly built under strict C11 `-O2` and used for
focused named-graph compile/result/rejection tests. Those successful builds/tests
are **not** a Bend benchmark or validation of the recovered optimization patches.

## Historical evidence and its limits

Supplied `2026-10-02-BEND-CHECKER-PERFORMANCE-RECOVERY.md` records:

- AP base `9146893`, artifact/readback/conversion candidate; principal experiments
  are not the current `solver_inputs` overlay.
- Bend2 `7d24b8d0235cb9781140512c0f163c48ea84a719`, v2.0.34, Bun 1.4.2;
  ordinary `--check-only`, not BendTT `--verdict`.
- A corresponding tree workload of 400 pairs / 800 concrete computational
  equalities, not universal tree properties. Different native proof encodings
  include startup, parse, elaboration and checking costs.
- Reported combined head/closure prototype: 183,131,801 steps; intermediate
  materialization calls/prefix copies drop to zero on that workload, while final
  required readback remains.
- Reported fresh historical comparison: AP median 6.959428s vs Bend 1.780815s,
  approximately 3.908x time and 21.2x RSS. **Not current-head measurements.**
- Original Core fixtures fail with the experimental interface/fuel changes;
  a test adapter subsequently passes adapted tests. Not an unchanged-suite pass.

The named `src/prototype/bend_benchmark/remaining_*` scripts, source workloads,
raw JSON, profiling output and patches are absent from fetched main and from
that path at the pinned revision, and were not supplied with the two Markdown
files. This limits reproducibility; it does not establish that the local
experiments never happened. We have not re-run the 400-pair comparison.

## Requested work

1. Recover/publish a runnable evidence bundle with source hashes, generators,
   AP/Bend pins, compiler/runtime flags, patches, raw timings, counters, RSS and
   original-vs-adapted test results. Remove fixed temporary-path assumptions.
2. Build a matched current-HEAD baseline for accepted and latest Prototype
   separately. Measure fresh processes, repeated interleaved timings, step
   counts, allocation/lifetime and reduction-category profiles.
3. Prototype narrow captured-head/closure delivery and direct IADT field
   application under `src/prototype/`; keep neutral/effectful fallbacks intact.
4. Independently measure temporary arena/index sizing and repeated projections;
   do not assert universal benefits from globally shrinking allocator defaults.
5. Investigate scheduler batching only with an explicit Effort/charging and
   checkpoint/wake contract; do not drop required verification to gain speed.

## Safety boundaries and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Correct captured environments and binder freshening under head delivery.
- [ ] Preserve rejection controls, neutral terms, effects, branch functions,
  total-result projection and independently checked evidence.
- [ ] Intermediate head readiness is not a completed normalization certificate;
  charge and validate required final readback, including low-budget suspension.
- [ ] Distinguish raw evaluator transitions from charged compilation Effort.
  If administrative step counts change, state the policy rather than hide it.
- [ ] Preserve one-shot/chunked agreement, FIFO/wake dependencies and checkpoint
  cuts under the selected policy; test fresh-process persistence round-trips.
- [ ] Document API/fuel-fixture migrations and add independent normative tests.
  Do not erase original failing controls or cite adapted tests as unchanged.
- [ ] Preserve full regression/acceptance gates; characterize pre-existing public
  reload failures separately instead of claiming they are solved by this work.
- [ ] Provide matched current-head measurements and retained-memory ownership
  evidence. Report overhead changes separately from universal speedup claims.

## Relationship to existing work

Related to #51 (reproducible semantic-owner/size gates) and #52 (checked equality
reuse), but neither replaces this workload-specific evaluator/readback recovery
investigation. This is not a request for broad caching, unsafe equality shortcuts,
partiality syntax, or immediate acceptance-source promotion.

## Supporting documents

The documentation-only [PR #58](https://github.com/repyt-margorp/a-program/pull/58)
contains the supplied performance report
and `doc/2026-10-03-NEW-AUDITS-CURRENT-HEAD-REVIEW.md`. Historical figures retain
their original provenance and are qualified by the current-head re-audit.
The PR documents this work; it does not implement or resolve it.
title: Recover and revalidate checker head/readback optimizations with Effort and persistence gates

body:
## Problem List

1. Specify and prototype reuse of one selected checked equality relation before introducing equality saturation or adaptive compilation policy.

## P1. Selected relation reuse with optional downstream compilation investment

### Subjective (User)

2026-10-01, English paraphrase: re-audit the supplied equality/adaptive-compilation document on latest A Program and submit appropriate Issues together with a two-document PR. The supplied philosophy treats native compilation as optional investment and keeps realization policy downstream.

No new wire format, e-graph, trusted checker, reflection rule or JIT syntax is approved by this Issue.

### Objective (Code)

Fresh main: `97825ec28506f8a055db18af9e2577cba8cb1da7`.

- conversion.c's local certificate contains left/right; conversion.h excludes equality reflection.
- derivation.c records local receipt endpoints and clears process-local certificate pointers; derivation_io.c rejects raw receipt pointers. synthesis_derivation.c re-establishes local authority. Language witnesses and semantic obligations already persist; it is incorrect to say all equality is discarded.
- Accepted images use APGSRC62/63 and ordinary Solve/reduction checking. The unpromoted artifact prototype uses APGSRC68/APGRET4 materialized typed views and an explicit input-only recomputation profile.
- C emission, LinkerScript and limited native scalar/nominal-enum profiles already exist as prototypes. General equality assets, an equality-saturation engine and adaptive hotness/JIT policy are not implemented by those facilities.
- The emitter does no Solve/conversion; its default adapter still checks whole-module obligations. --trust-image is explicit **unauthenticated user trust**, not proof reuse.
- Current solver_inputs work removes duplicated adapters/result owners; full SE1-SE5 and public resumption remain open.

Fresh accepted/prototype ordinary checks, adapted artifact semantic checks, and C backend/scalar differentials pass. The public strict fuel-partition gate still fails. No full acceptance/sanitized/backend-correctness theorem is claimed.

### Assessment

Keep this separate from existing work:
- #44: artifact-to-C semantic boundary;
- #47: relevance and partial-artifact admissibility;
- #49: target-native lowering;
- existing SE/AP plans: ownership and exact frontier restoration.

Start with one existing **closed, well-typed, pure-total DefEq** transformation, not a broad new relation DB or e-graph. Reuse derivation/reduction protocols and actual typed owners where possible.

Kernel DefEq, higher Identity, type equivalence, representation relations and target observational equivalence are different permissions. An optimizer quotient is not automatically source truncation; the forbidden shortcut is letting arbitrary Identity endpoint union extend Kernel conversion or erase computational witness information. A future explicitly validated target-observational/irrelevant fragment may use Identity-derived rewrites.

Type preservation alone does not establish behavioral preservation. Checking the selected relation does not itself verify the C emitter/runtime/native compiler. Keep those end-to-end trust assumptions explicit.

A .a format extension needs an independent A Program consumer, not only a backend preference. Persist selected immutable semantic obligations/explanations when justified, not union-find/search history or another mutable equality answer.

For downstream policy let I include search, validation, lowering, native build and cache/profile I/O; d/n denote direct/native invocation costs under the same contract. Investment is justified only if d > n and expected_remaining_runs*(d-n) > I. This is a heuristic, not a universal speedup claim.

### Plan

- [ ] Specify the relation endpoints, Context/classifier, nominal identity, observer contract, side conditions and validator.
- [ ] Implement a narrow unpromoted reuse experiment against existing semantic roots and receipt/derivation/reduction APIs.
- [ ] Round-trip only selected reachable obligations and revalidate them; reject corrupt endpoints, scopes, classifiers, nominal identities, premises and target profiles.
- [ ] Reuse the checked result before selected C lowering; preserve a no-optimization path and input-image immutability.
- [ ] Test computational higher witnesses/loops and same-Core/different-classifier controls; no blanket proof erasure or equality reflection.
- [ ] Measure source search versus import/validation/lowering time, fuel, bytes and memory.
- [ ] Only after this boundary works, prototype optional external profile/LinkerScript cost policy; profile/native caches must be semantically discardable.
- [ ] Never skip required validation to meet a cost budget; skip the optional optimization instead.
- [ ] Keep partiality, general relevance, full frontier checkpointing, CUDA/RTL and full equality saturation as separate milestones.

Completion: one selected checked relation can be reused with a documented trust contract and measured cost, without copying source authority. Adaptive policy may choose realization/cost, never source truth or acceptance.

Detailed re-audit (including primary-source spot-checks and qualifications to the original design) will be included under:
`doc/2026-09-29-EQUALITY-BEARING-ARTIFACTS-ADAPTIVE-COMPILATION-AUDIT.md`
in the companion two-document PR.
title: Design: checked equality reuse before adaptive compilation and equality saturation

## Problem List

1. P1 — Define runtime relevance and compilation admissibility without treating unfinished evidence as accepted authority.

## P1. Erasure and compilation from partially verified artifacts

### Subjective (User)

2026-09-29, English paraphrase: the user approved separating this topic from the linkable-component implementation issue and submitting both with the supplied document.
The proposed default pending-proof policy is a design question to resolve, not an implemented or automatically approved acceptance rule.

### Objective (Code)

Baseline: main at `ea287c2e45d33c6d19f34faca6ab9fd61fc50be5`.

- The C prototype adapter currently requires ordinary whole-module checking or explicitly trusted saved whole-module completion.
- The emitter itself does not check imported occurrences or establish relevance.
- Prototype README/runtime implement selected Identity actions and scoped transports; arbitrary paths are not blanket-erased.
- Existing unused/lazy operands and supported Identity reductions do not establish a general relevance judgment for pending artifacts.
- Review-session check-c-backend passed. No proposed erasure pass, pending-proof acceptance mode or cross-language erasure theorem was tested.

### Assessment

Distinguish three obligations:
1. Is an argument/field computationally irrelevant?
2. Are the runtime types, effects, representations and boundary contracts established without the pending obligation?
3. Is the requested target realization supported?

Absence of a proof object from generated code does not establish (2). A proof may justify an impossible branch, a cast/layout, a bounds check removal or an index equality even if its runtime payload disappears.
Require a dependency/accounting rule identifying which unresolved obligations are irrelevant to the selected compilation claim. Never classify an unknown typing obligation as proof-only by naming or syntax.

A Program must not adopt Lean Prop-style erasure by analogy alone. The existing higher/path/Identity behavior may be relevant; decide per permitted eliminator/occurrence what can be erased and prove or check the criterion.
The supplied document already warns against unsafe optimization from pending evidence; this issue makes that warning an admission prerequisite, not only an optimizer switch.

Keep verification status, runtime completeness and lowering correctness separate. Metadata records assumptions but does not make them sound.
Pending semantic claims can remain recorded while a separately justified conservative runtime graph is emitted; insufficient typing/layout information stays NOT_READY, unless an explicit, separately specified assumption or runtime-hole mode applies.
Recheckable relevance facts must not require trusting all completion bytes.
No general theorem prover need be embedded in generated C.

Existing link packaging can proceed using current admission rules. This broader feature follows #44's partial-artifact direction but is not required to split main or generate a library.

### Plan

- [ ] Specify a conservative relevance judgment, its trusted base, and dependency relation to typing/conversion/layout/effect obligations.
- [ ] Distinguish runtime-relevant data, compile-time representation inputs and erasable evidence; do not assume proof irrelevance/UIP.
- [ ] Specify Identity/transport cases whose erasure is justified; retain or reject unsupported relevant cases.
- [ ] Define selected-export admissibility from partial artifacts independently of whole-program completion, with explicit residual obligations.
- [ ] Decide development/release defaults only after the criterion and negative tests exist.
- [ ] Prohibit pending evidence from authorizing unreachable, unchecked casts, narrowing or check removal.
- [ ] Separate optional computational-hole traps from erased proof obligations; give traps an explicit changed-behavior contract.
- [ ] Test harmless pending theorem versus pending representation/type constraint; same erased witness behavior; computational witness preservation; invalid siblings/dependency closure; false bounds and equality assumptions.
- [ ] Record verification, assumptions, relevance status and runtime holes in receipts without granting Kernel evidence.

Completion: a precisely specified class of partially verified exports compiles under checked admissibility conditions, unsafe dependencies reject or require explicit policy, and the generated program is not misreported as fully verified.
title: Design runtime relevance and safe compilation admissibility for partial artifacts

# Open question: computation-level general recursion and loop syntax

Date: 2026-09-28
Fresh baseline: `main` at `e7162320712f1acdc9420b6ffae993cd97035663` (independent clone under a-book; no implementation edits).
Status: proposal/review, not implemented by this submission.

## Problem List

1. P1 — Add potentially infinite computation without weakening the value/proof boundary, induction, or synthesis-first typing.

## P1. General recursion at the computation boundary

### Subjective (User)

English paraphrase of the current 2026-09-28 request: open a discussion issue for introducing infinite-loop syntax and the supporting system. Submit the two supplied recursion/empty-type notes together with the backend audit in one documentation PR.
Earlier user statements quoted in those documents are supplied-document provenance, not independently reconstructed conversation records. No final token or operational rule is approved here.

### Objective (Code)

- README keeps `*k` induction-derived, declaration names non-recursive, and `::` post-synthesis.
- `src/classifier.h:25` separates effect rows and totality. TOTAL assumes admissible inputs and returning effect interpretations; UNSPECIFIED is not evidence of divergence.
- `src/evidence.c:3462` (`pg_prove_termination`) still requires an already-TOTAL suspended computation. This is not a post-hoc proof principle for arbitrary partial computation.
- `src/evidence.c:4121` (`pg_prove_total_pure_value`) requires TOTAL and an empty effect row.
- The inspected CLI/source contracts do not provide the proposed AGAIN construct. The notes describe a proposed extension, not a demonstrated current compiler defect.
- Fresh `make -s -j3 check-execution` passed: checked entry, handlers, repeat/split invocation, cancellation, source/image execution, exact bytes, effect order and I/O failure.
- Existing typed/scoped transport tests also passed; these do not test new recursion syntax.

### Assessment

Recommended architectural boundary: add general recurrence on the computation side, preserve the existing total IADT/Acc recursion, and keep potentially partial forcing out of dependent conversion and proof introduction.

The supplied notes leave important choices open:

1. Is self an explicit thunk or an implicit force operation? Which lexical binder introduces it? Does recurrence permit non-tail calls, or only tail iteration?
2. What environment is reused? Re-entering a closed thunk captures the same lexical values; rebinding a local variable does not automatically update the next iteration. Define loop-carried arguments/state and nested-loop targeting explicitly. The changing-n examples in the report are pseudocode, not an implemented state discipline.
3. How do normal-return paths determine result type while effects and totality are synthesized separately? AGAIN is only a placeholder.
4. Is a result-less computation classified using an ordinary empty value type, a separate no-return classifier, or another explicit mechanism? Preserve post-synthesis `::`; do not introduce hidden expected-type retagging.
5. How are effect handlers, resumptions, cancellation and observable traces treated? UNSPECIFIED alone must not determine any of these.
6. Is termination recovery elaboration into existing Acc/induction, or genuine post-hoc totalization? The latter needs a new sound evidence rule, not removal of the existing guard.
7. What representation supports operational unfolding without introducing unguarded proof-level cycles or requiring a new Core node prematurely?

Empty elimination requires a value of the empty type; runtime failure and divergence do not. A computation with empty normal-result type cannot normally return in a sound model, but may fail or exit through effects. It entails divergence only with extra assumptions excluding such outcomes. A thunk of a partial computation is a value, but not a proof that forcing it terminates.

Primary-source spot-check: Levy's thesis §5.3.1 adds divergence/recursion as computation constructs with a thunked self binder. It does not choose A Program's synthesis policy or empty-result convention. [Levy thesis](https://www.cs.bham.ac.uk/~pbl/papers/thesisqmwphd.pdf).
The supplied wider bibliography was not exhaustively reverified.

### Plan

- [ ] Agree on operational rules and lexical/state behavior before choosing syntax.
- [ ] Specify result/effect/totality synthesis and branch joining.
- [ ] Specify conversion and logical consistency invariants.
- [ ] Design any termination-recovery rule separately.
- [ ] Prototype and test pure recurrence, printing recurrence, conditional return, changing loop state, nested recurrence and handler interaction.
- [ ] Add negative tests: no closed empty proof from divergence, no UNSPECIFIED-to-TOTAL cast, no contextual rewrite of synthesized type through `::`.
- [ ] Test bounded execution/cancellation without calling a budget exhaustion proof of divergence.

Completion for this Open Question: reviewed rules, explicit decisions and a scoped implementation plan. Documentation acceptance alone does not implement recursion.
title: Open question: computation-level general recursion, loop syntax and logical boundaries

# Generic finite-container sorting: current verification and design audit

Date: 2026-09-27
Status: design proposal; existing List prerequisites verified, proposed container interfaces not implemented or checked.
Code baseline: main at `2a67ac3e6387ca30506a8ba81400819eb1831b00` (clean implementation checkout).
Related: #39 and #40 (local/strong sortedness foundation); this proposal does not reopen the resolved sortedness distinction.

## Problem List

1. **P1 — Define the semantic and operational boundaries of sorting finite containers**, without conflating finiteness, ordered traversal, lawful reconstruction, and native random-access capability.

## P1. Finite sorting beyond the current List backend

### Subjective (User)

English paraphrase of the user's 2026-09-27 request: submit the supplied generic-container sorting audit as an Issue and documentation PR; organizing how finite objects are sorted is important.

The user has not selected a particular dictionary, public name, permutation convention, implementation technique, or new language primitive. The interface names below are proposals from the supplied audit, not user-approved requirements.

### Objective (Code)

Fresh checks at the pinned revision:

- `tests/fixtures/sorted-proof-provider.p` provides the List/SizedList-based sorting foundation.
- `tests/fixtures/local-strong-sorted.p` defines local sortedness separately and aliases the existing stronger relation as `general_strongly_sorted`.
- `tests/acceptance/generic-quick-local-sorted-result.p` proves the ordinary QuickSort result locally sorted using directional comparator evidence. The strong-result proof additionally uses transitivity.
- `tests/fixtures/generic_sorted/content-proof.p` defines an inductive permutation relation with nil, keep, swap, and composition. The result theorem in `content-result-proof.p` relates the input to the actual QuickSort output, not merely a membership set. Duplicate multiplicities matter.
- The implementation is generic in element type/comparison but these theorems use a particular List representation. SizedList is used in the termination machinery; it is not already a generic container abstraction.
- A scoped search of test `.p` and compiler `.c` sources found none of the proposed names `FiniteContents`, `FiniteLinearView`, `sortToList`, `sortWithin`, `sortPermutation`, `IndexedSortKernel`. This does not prove equivalent encodings are impossible.
- README documents the current merge implementation as repeated insertion. A conventional two-front MergeSort complexity claim is not justified by that implementation.

Verification:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `make -s pointer-check` | Pass |
| `bash tests/quick_result.sh build/pointer/pointer-check` | Pass, including negative, image reload and resume controls |
| Generic local ordinary-result theorem | Pass; 1,054,265 checker steps |
| Derived strong ordinary-result theorem | Pass; 1,087,230 checker steps |
| Generic QuickSort permutation-result theorem | Pass; 2,504,960 checker steps |

The last three checks used `--legacy-intrinsic-dot --steps 10000000 --imports PROVIDER SOURCE`.
Providers were assembled from existing repository fixtures, with import directive lines removed from appended modules:
base = sorted-proof-provider + local-strong-sorted + quick-sort-proof-common.
The local check used this base; the strong check appended generic-quick-local-sorted-result;
the content check appended generic-quick-sorted-result to the base, and checked the concatenation of
acceptance/generic-quick-sorted.p, fixtures/generic_sorted/content-proof.p and content-result-proof.p.
No theorem body was modified.

These are **prerequisite tests**, not proofs that the proposed view wrappers compile.
The full acceptance suite, sanitizer suite, new container implementations, and performance comparisons were not run.
Checker transition counts are not sorting runtime complexity measurements.

### Assessment

This is a design/library-extension issue, not a newly reproduced compiler bug.

Separate three questions:

1. **Sort into a List:** choose an observation `contents : X -> List A`, then apply a certified List backend.
2. **Sort within the original shape:** additionally provide lawful same-length reconstruction and prove shape/index preservation.
3. **Sort positions:** choose finite ordered positions, produce a bijection of positions, and act on the original representation.

A finite object does not by itself choose a traversal, ranking, or reconstruction operation.
Even a type-correct `contents` function can omit intended contents; adequacy must be specified against the intended model.
Strict positivity of an IADT does not establish any of these sorting laws.

A reasonable experiment is a proof-carrying backend with `sort`, a specified local or strong sortedness theorem, and a permutation theorem; stability and cost remain separate properties.
Do not erase the newly implemented local/strong distinction or demand a total-order package for every theorem.

For a linear view, require:
- contents after reconstruction equal the requested replacement sequence;
- shape/index preservation;
- reconstruction of original contents agrees observationally with the original;
- the selected traversal accounts for each intended position exactly once.

Start with homogeneous List and SizedList/Vec-like representations. Arbitrary dependent positions may hold different types, so not every same-length replacement is legal. Do not assume proof irrelevance or independence from length-equality witnesses without establishing it.

A value-list permutation theorem and a position bijection are related but not interchangeable:
duplicates and labels can distinguish positions with equal values. Fix the direction of the position map explicitly (for example, new position to old position).

Independent reference spot-check: Mathlib's `Tuple.sort` returns an `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` for a tuple `Fin n -> A` under a linear order; `Tuple.monotone_sort` states monotonicity after reindexing. This is a concrete permutation-first precedent, not evidence that its assumptions or implementation transfer unchanged to A Program. [Mathlib Tuple.Sort documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Fin/Tuple/Sort.html).
This source was inspected; Lean was not executed.

Native indexed comparison/swap capabilities are a separate operational interface. Do not force linked lists into a random-access model, or infer complexity/stability from semantic view laws.

Adopted here: preserve the audit and expose these alternatives for review.
Deferred: public API selection, compiler changes, automatic derivation for arbitrary IADTs, coinductive/infinite sorting, and performance claims.

### Plan

- [x] Recheck current List-based sortedness and permutation prerequisites at a pinned revision.
- [x] Separate current observations from historical claims and untested proposals.
- [ ] Prototype sort-to-List with a specified finite contents observation and a certified backend.
- [ ] Prototype same-shape transport for List and one genuinely indexed homogeneous representation; prove the reconstruction laws.
- [ ] Compare this with finite-position permutation plus a lawful representation action before selecting the public interface.
- [ ] Add positive and negative law tests: omitted/duplicated positions, incorrect refill, wrong length, shape change, and duplicate elements.
- [ ] Specify traversal choices for trees and key/payload behavior for maps before claiming either supported.
- [ ] Measure representation-specific runtime and proof/checking costs separately if performance is in scope.

Completion for a later implementation: two distinct representations reuse the backend with checked sortedness and occurrence-preserving permutation, with all required view/action laws explicit and no unjustified arbitrary-container claim.
This documentation PR itself does not complete that implementation plan.

## Provenance and precedence

The supplied audit below is retained as a historical research record. Its SHA-256 before inclusion was
`3256054f6ccd70908ed8364174be84e7871750f368eac00a772bb2e0799ff807`.
Its older snapshot references and broad cross-language survey are not all independently revalidated by this submission.
In particular, the fresh local/strong observations above supersede any older description that treats that split as pending.
Sketch interfaces and pseudocode in the supplied report are not newly accepted syntax or tested implementations.
The addendum above is the active work list; historical recommendations below are review material, not additional approved commitments.

## Supplied audit (preserved)
title: Design audit: finite-container sorting, lawful views and position permutations
